summary: Partial, evidence-backed mapping of NumberFieldArithmetic against five core supplier/consumer roadmaps: 19 dependency links and four ownership-overlap recommendations. All eight source stages were read. Exhaustive atlas coverage is NOT complete; this is a resumable draft, not an integration-ready result.

baseline.declarationVerification: No declaration-level baseline claims; roadmap inventories are not independent verification.

links.reason: Local finite-extension uniqueness, integer-ring/integral-closure structures and intrinsic e/f supply the canonical completion adapters in 5.2, 5.5 and 5.7. The theorem supplies no reverse polynomial-roadmap dependency and no finite-prime certificate of containment in a proper subgroup.

evidence.quote:
Membership: `v ∈ ramifiedSupport K L` if and only if
  `v.asIdeal ∣ relDiscr (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L)`, if and only if some prime of `𝓞 L` over `v` is ramified.
Construct the finite set `ramifiedPrimes K L` and prove that its complement is the union above.

overlaps.detail: NFA 4.3 defines the finite set of ramified base primes by relative-discriminant support. Chebotarev 2 asks for the same set under ramifiedPrimes, with an additional Artin-fibre complement theorem.
overlaps.proposal: Make ramifiedPrimes an abbreviation of ramifiedSupport or prove a named equality immediately; import its membership/finiteness API. Keep the union-of-Frobenius-fibres theorem and later exceptional-set operations in Chebotarev. Do not make ramifiedSupport depend on any Artin map.

overlaps.detail: Both stages discuss the normal-closure action, embeddings/root cosets, point stabilizers and degree. NFA 7.1 starts with an abstract finite extension and NormalClosureData; PolynomialGaloisGroups 0 starts with a separable polynomial and Polynomial.Gal.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the distinct field and polynomial interfaces, share generic normal-closure/embedding-action lemmas below both, and prove the minimal-polynomial comparison on the polynomial side. Respect the polynomial roadmap's explicit one-declaration exchange: do not add a reverse dependency to NFA or move nTj classification into NFA.

overlaps.detail: NFA 3.1–3.3 treat the index and discriminant of a primitive integral element's power order; GNF 11 treats arbitrary number-field orders, their conductor, index and discriminant. These agree only after specializing the general order to Z[theta]; field generation and finite index cannot be dropped.
overlaps.proposal: Keep NFA's primitive-element input and its index/exponent distinctions. Use shared determinant/index lemmas for the specialization of NumberFieldOrder to a power order, with a named comparison. Leave nonmaximal-order Picard carriers and all proper-versus-invertible issues in GNF; do not make NFA's early splitting API depend on the full order/Picard development.

overlaps.detail: NFA 2.6 identifies rational cyclotomic Frobenius with p modulo the conductor. Chebotarev 4 states the cyclotomic Frobenius action over an arbitrary number-field base and builds character weights.
overlaps.proposal: Reuse NFA's finite-level arithmetic Frobenius and the rational identification. Retain the general-base root-of-unity action, conductor comparison and character weights in Chebotarev. A rational p-mod-n calculation alone is not the general-base theorem; never insert an inverse.

gaps.detail: NFA 5.6 says an IsArithFrobAt element maps to the local Frobenius. LF Layer 2 frobeniusAlgEquiv has unramified Galois hypotheses; the ramified branch supplies only a coset modulo inertia. A separate LF2→NFA5 edge is deferred until that exact branch is recorded or clarified; do not infer a canonical element at a ramified prime.

Chebotarev 12.1 says deletion of finite Euler factors preserves the Dedekind-zeta residue. The residue is instead multiplied by the finite product of (1 - Norm(p)^(-1)); only the coefficient 1 of the logarithmic-derivative pole is unchanged. GNF 3E explicitly records the Euler correction. This source issue does not change the arithmetic links and needs a separate upstream correction.
